working_title: He Came Home From Iraq Unable to Breathe. Nineteen Years Later He Still Has No Judgment.
one_line: Texas state trooper Le Roy Torres was deployed to Iraq in 2007, came home with constrictive bronchitis from the burn pits, asked his own employer for a job he could physically do, was refused -- and the State of Texas answered his lawsuit by saying it could not be sued at all.
contradiction: The federal law that guarantees a returning soldier his job back was met by his own state employer's argument that no soldier could enforce it against a state -- and after he won that argument in the Supreme Court and then won a jury verdict, an appellate court took the verdict away again in 2026.
scored_by: claude, 2026-08-12, v002 rubric, for the 45-minute slot

justification.personal_relevance: A job and an employer who will not accommodate an illness -- broad. But the entry point is a deployment, and most viewers have not had one. 10.
justification.wtf_factor: A state telling a returning soldier it is immune from the statute written for him is a real 'that is allowed?'. It is a legal surprise rather than a physical one, so 11.
justification.human_stakes: Career, lungs and nineteen years, and the lungs do not come back. 13.
justification.contradiction: Served, injured by the service, refused by the employer the service protected him from -- and the win at the top court did not end it. 13.
justification.story_arc: The best-documented long arc on the slate, and it is still moving: 2007 deployment, 2009 reemployment, diagnosis, 2017 suit, 2022 Supreme Court win, jury verdict, and a Fifteenth Court of Appeals reversal on 7 May 2026. 10.
justification.title_power: True and heavy, but it needs 'no judgment' explained, and the rubric penalises a title that needs a footnote. 8.
justification.thumbnail_power: Hardest of the eight to carry in one image -- lungs, a uniform and a courthouse are three subjects, not one. 7.
justification.evidence: Two published opinions retrieved in full (597 U.S. 580 and No. 15-24-00089-CV) plus public-domain oral-argument audio. 10.
justification.broad_audience: Veterans land squarely inside a base that is 92.5% male and 77% aged 55+, which is reach into the existing audience rather than beyond it. 8.
justification.franchiseability: Burn pits, Camp Lejeune, Agent Orange, PACT Act denials -- a real family of stories, but the channel's own EP57-59 slate already holds Lejeune. 4.
justification.real_footage: Supreme Court oral-argument audio, No. 20-603, 29 March 2022 -- public domain, and present in the shelf's Oyez index as 'torres v texas department of public safety -> [[2021, 20-603]]'.
justification.major_reversal: Lost in the Texas appellate court, won unanimously enough at the Supreme Court to be revived, won at trial, and lost the verdict again on 7 May 2026.
